name: Nimbus ERP for WooCommerce
author: Derian Pinto

sections.description:
Nimbus ERP for WooCommerce connects your online store with Nimbus ERP, the business management system by Codegea. Every paid order arrives in the ERP as a sale — ready to confirm or already invoiced — and the store always shows the real stock of your warehouse. No more typing orders twice, no more selling what you do not have.

Products, prices, photos, brands, categories and stock travel from the ERP to the store through the WooCommerce REST API. This plugin covers the other direction: what happens in the store goes back to the ERP.

Orders that arrive as sales

  • Every paid order is sent to the ERP as a sale. You choose how it arrives: as a draft to review, as a confirmed sale (stock is deducted) or confirmed and invoiced.
  • Taxes (VAT), coupons and shipping are sent exactly as charged, so the ERP sale adds up to what the customer paid.
  • Choose which order statuses send the order (Processing, Completed, On hold). An order placed by bank transfer arrives as a draft and is confirmed when it is paid — never duplicated.
  • Re-send any order from its screen: Order actions → Enviar al ERP.

Stock you can trust

  • Pick the ERP warehouse (main store, branch…) that store orders are taken from.
  • Optionally, stock changes made by hand in WooCommerce (editing a product, a CSV import) are passed back to the ERP. The plugin sends the change (+3, −2), not the new value, so a sale made in the ERP that the store has not received yet is never overwritten. Each change is applied only once, even when it is retried.
  • Stock reductions caused by orders and changes made by the ERP itself are never sent back, so nothing is counted twice and there are no loops.
  • Sales, purchases and adjustments made in the ERP reach the store within a minute. This is done by Nimbus ERP through the WooCommerce REST API when stock sync is turned on in the ERP, not by this plugin.

Newsletter signups

  • Optional “subscribe to our newsletter” checkbox at checkout — works with the classic and the block checkout.
  • [nimbus_erp_newsletter] shortcode with a signup form for any page, post or widget.
  • Double opt-in: the ERP sends a confirmation email before anyone is subscribed, and stores the consent text the customer accepted.

Built to be reliable

  • Orders, stock changes and newsletter signups are sent in the background with Action Scheduler (bundled with WooCommerce), so the checkout never waits for the ERP.
  • If the ERP does not accept a send, orders and stock changes are retried after 1, 5, 15, 60 and 180 minutes, and newsletter signups after 1, 5 and 15 minutes when the ERP does not answer.
  • Every request is signed with HMAC-SHA256 using a secret shared with your ERP.
  • A send log with the last 50 operations helps you diagnose problems without server access.
  • Compatible with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS).

Requirements

  • WooCommerce 8.0 or newer.
  • A Nimbus ERP account with the WordPress / WooCommerce plugin enabled. The plugin does nothing on its own.

The settings screens are in Spanish.

External services

This plugin connects to the Nimbus ERP instance configured by the store owner (WooCommerce → Nimbus ERP → Conexión). Nothing is sent until an ERP address and secret are saved.

  • What is sent and when
    • When an order reaches one of the selected statuses: order number, status, payment method, currency, billing name, email, phone and tax ID, line items (SKU, quantity, prices, discount, tax rate), coupons used, shipping cost and total, the shipping method, the shipping address (name, company, address, city, state, postcode, country and phone; the billing address when the order has no shipping address), and the customer note.
    • When stock is changed by hand in WooCommerce (only if enabled): product SKU, how much the stock changed and a random ID for that change.
    • When a customer ticks the newsletter checkbox at checkout or submits the newsletter form (only if used): email, name, the consent text they accepted and their IP address.
    • When testing the connection: the store URL and the plugin version.
  • Where: {ERP address}/api/plugins/wordpress/webhook/{ping|orders|stock|newsletter}, signed with HMAC-SHA256 using the shared secret.
  • Service provider: Codegea — terms of service: https://codegea.com/en/terms-of-service — privacy policy: https://codegea.com/en/privacy-policy
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (WooCommerce must be active).
  2. In Nimbus ERP, open Configuración → Plugins → WordPress / WooCommerce → Pedidos and copy the ERP address and the secret.
  3. In WordPress, go to WooCommerce → Nimbus ERP → Conexión, paste them and click «Conectar con el ERP».
  4. In the Pedidos and Stock tabs, choose how orders arrive and which ERP warehouse they are taken from.

That’s it: the next paid order shows up in the ERP.
sections.faq:
Does it work without Nimbus ERP?

No. It only sends data to a Nimbus ERP account. Contact Codegea to get one.

Can an order be duplicated in the ERP?

No. The ERP identifies each order by its WooCommerce ID, so re-sending it is safe. If an order was sent unpaid (e.g. bank transfer on hold) and is paid later, the ERP confirms that same sale.

Are stock reductions sent twice?

No. Stock reductions caused by orders are not sent: the ERP deducts them when it receives the order. Changes made by the ERP itself are not sent back either.

What happens if the ERP is offline?

Orders, stock changes and newsletter signups wait in the queue and are retried automatically (see Built to be reliable above for the schedule). You can see every attempt in the Registro tab.

Can the ERP issue the electronic invoice?

Yes. With the «Confirmar y facturar» mode the ERP confirms the sale and issues the invoice, as long as the customer entered a tax ID (cédula/RUC) and invoicing is set up in the ERP.

I used the plugin when it was called «Codegea ERP». Do I lose my settings?

No. Version 1.2.0 copies the connection, warehouse and send log of the old plugin, keeps orders already sent from being sent again, and the old [codegea_erp_newsletter] shortcode still works. You can delete the old plugin afterwards.
sections.changelog:
1.4.0

  • Orders carry the shipping address and the shipping method, so the ERP can dispatch them (or prepare a store pickup) and print the shipping label.
  • Works with Nimbus ERP shipping: when the ERP ships or delivers an order, it adds an order note with the tracking number and completes the order through the WooCommerce REST API (this is done by the ERP, not by this plugin).

1.3.0

  • Manual stock changes are sent to the ERP as the amount that changed (+3, −2) instead of the new value, so a sale made in the ERP that the store has not received yet is never overwritten.
  • Stock changes the ERP does not accept are retried automatically (1, 5, 15, 60 and 180 minutes), each with its own ID so the ERP applies it only once.
  • Needs an up-to-date Nimbus ERP.

1.2.2

  • Stock changes sent to the ERP carry the time they were read, so a late or retried update can no longer overwrite a newer stock value.

1.2.1

  • Settings screens with the Nimbus look: logo, orange accent on tabs, buttons and options.

1.2.0

  • Renamed from «Codegea ERP» to «Nimbus ERP for WooCommerce». Settings, send log and sent orders of an existing Codegea ERP install are kept, and the old [codegea_erp_newsletter] shortcode still works.

1.1.0

  • Newsletter: optional checkbox at checkout (classic and block checkout) and the [codegea_erp_newsletter] signup form shortcode, both with double opt-in through the ERP.
  • Orders now include the coupons used and their discount, so the ERP can count coupon uses (Loyalty plugin).

1.0.0

  • First release: orders (draft, confirm, invoice), stock in both directions, connection test, warehouse selection and send log.

screenshots.caption: Connection: paste the ERP address and secret once and see which company and warehouse the store works with.
Orders: choose whether a paid order arrives as a draft, a confirmed sale or a confirmed and invoiced sale, and which statuses send it.
Stock: pick the ERP warehouse that store orders are taken from and decide whether manual stock changes go back to the ERP.
Newsletter: offer a signup checkbox at checkout and a shortcode form, with double opt-in through the ERP.
